post.caption: Michelangelo's David once wore gold. In 1504, Florence set the marble giant beside its town hall. Michelangelo gilded his sling and the tree trunk behind his leg. A gilded wreath crowned his head. Florence added a gilded garland of 28 copper leaves, to cover him. None of that gold survives today. In 2002, conservators found rough patches where gold once stuck. The V&A's plaster copy got a fig leaf instead of a garland. In 1873, the marble David moved indoors to the Accademia. He stands 5.17 meters tall, with no gold left.
